text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fuel supply to Mosimi and Ejigbo depots near Lagos disrupted by pipeline damage; long queues at pump stations persist.
- Candidates for March 15 municipal elections emerge; candidates for chairperson to be selected at primaries on Wednesday.
- Umbrella association of Nigerian chambers of commerce reiterates call for merger of dual exchange rates, saying current policy presents wrong picture of budget surpluses.
- Imminent increase in capital base requirement for mortgage institutions makes operators jittery.
- A computerised Customs Processing Centre takes off for the major seaports around Lagos; customs chief Brigadier-General Samuel Ango says target is customs clearance within 48 hours.
- Politicians scuffle at ward congresses to select candidates for next month's local council elections.
- Government officials, U.N. official parley over expected visit of two U.N. rapporteurs to Nigeria on a mission to investigate the judicial system.
- Government cautions universities against increasing fees until an official position on the controversial issue is taken.
- About 2.49 billion naira has been spent on the 85 percent completed export processing zone in Calabar in the southeast and 981 million naira is needed to complete project, sources say.
- Shell appoints Nigerian engineer Egbert Imomoh deputy managing director of its joint venture with state-run NNPC which pumps half of Nigeria's crude oil output.
- Two killed in clashes at party primary in Jos central Nigeria to choose candidates for next month's municipal polls.
- Liquidity in banking system rekindles interest in shares.
